newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh MP demands sacking of Home Minister.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh MP demands sacking of Home Minister.

text.p: A simmering dispute in the Bangladesh government flared up on Wednesday when a ruling Awami League member of parliament (MP) demanded that Home Minister Rafiqul Islam be sacked.
"Not only has he failed to run his ministry but (he has) also contributed to (the) deteriorating law and order situation," Abdul Kader Siddiqi told a news conference.
Siddiqi said he had no dispute with Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina but wanted her to "fire her inefficient home minister".

His attack on the minister followed a raid by police and paramilitary troops on his ancestral home in the northern district of Tangail last week, when his younger brother, Azad Siddiqi, was arrested for alleged acts of terrorism. Azad Siddiqi denies the charges.

Known to many as "Tiger Siddiqi" for his deeds as a guerilla fighter in Bangladesh's 1971 war of independence against Pakistan, Kader Siddiqi said on Wednesday he had decided to discard a gallantry award he received for his role in the war.
"It's useless to keep an award which the nation itself has failed to honour," he said.
Government sources said Siddiqi regarded the arrest of his brother as a personal vendetta. "The action was intended to defame me and my family," he told reporters.
There was no immediate reaction from Hasina or the home minister, but political analysts said Siddiqi's move might lead to a stormy debate when parliament begins its winter session on January 15.

The main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), headed by Hasina's predecessor Begum Khaleda Zia, boycotted the last session of parliament in protest against what it said was the ruling party's refusal to allow opposition MPs to speak.
Parliament sources said there was still no sign that BNP would participate in the coming session.
"The opposition may now use the battle between Siddiqi and Islam to focus on alleged failures by Hasina's government," one source said on Wednesday.
Islam, a retired army major, was one of the four top sector commanders in the war of independence.
